ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a purple composite polygon, divided into upper and lower parts by a pink dashed horizontal line. The upper part is in the shape of a parallelogram, the top side is labeled 21, and the pink dashed vertical height from the top side to the bottom dividing line is labeled 14. The lower part is in the shape of a trapezoid, the bottom side is labeled 24, and the pink dashed vertical height from the dividing line to the bottom side is labeled 8. The base of the upper parallelogram and the upper base of the lower trapezoid are the same dividing line; because opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal, the length of this common base equals the top side 21. Then reason: Area of the upper parallelogram = base × height = 21×14=294. The two parallel bases of the lower trapezoid are 21 and 24 respectively, and the height is 8, so the area = ((21+24)/2)×8=45/2×8=180. Total area = 294+180=474. Rounded as required to the nearest tenth, it is 474.0.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a composite figure divided by the dashed horizontal segment. The upper part is a parallelogram: its top base is labeled 21, and the dashed vertical height down to the dividing line is labeled 14, so its area is 21×14. The lower part is a trapezoid: its parallel bases are the shared dashed segment, equal to 21 because it is the opposite side of the upper parallelogram, and the bottom base labeled 24; its height is labeled 8. Compute the trapezoid area as ((21+24)/2)×8. Add the two areas: 21×14 + ((21+24)/2)×8 = 294 + 180 = 474, then round to the nearest tenth if required.
